items.text: Single-window mode: closing a workspace now hands the same window to the one shown before it.
Single-window mode: +list now names every workspace, and focusing a parked one switches to it.
Single-window mode: a parked workspace waiting on a question now asks for attention, and the window reports the most urgent workspace.
Single-window mode: a workspace you switched away from now draws nothing, and catches up at once when shown.
Single-window mode: a workspace you are not looking at is kept at the window's size, so it is ready the moment you switch to it.
Single-window mode: a new window opened by hand comes up inside the one window, and switching to a workspace puts the cursor in its pane before anything is drawn.
Single-window mode: a new tab opens a workspace, the go-to-tab keys walk the workspaces in sidebar order, and a workspace shows no tab strip.
Single-window mode: a relaunch brings every workspace back inside the one window, with the one you were looking at on show.
Single-window mode: a saved window with several tabs comes back as one workspace per tab.
Single-window mode: switching workspaces fades the window's gradient from the old workspace's to the new one's.
Single-window mode: a click in the sidebar's all-windows list switches workspaces, and the one switched to keeps the sidebar you set.
A pane's banner and other popups now move with it to its new window, so closing the window it left no longer destroys them.
